questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error . India wants more stringent (A) / data storage rules so it can (B) / good access data and conduct (C) / investigations when the need arises. (D)
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

India wants more stringent (A) / data storage rules so it can (B) / good access data and conduct (C) / investigations when the need arises. (D)
questions.solution:
• 'easily access data' or 'access data efficiently' will be used instead of 'good access data' because there is a grammatical error. "Good access data" is incorrect, while "easily access data" or "access data efficiently" conveys the intended meaning; Like—
The new software allows researchers to easily access data for analysis.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error . The trade disputes have lead to (A) / higher tariffs by the two countries (B) / and created unease over (C) / the depth of their security alliance. (D)
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The trade disputes have lead to (A) / higher tariffs by the two countries (B) / and created unease over (C) / the depth of their security alliance. (D)
questions.solution:
• 'led' will be used instead of 'lead' because there is a verb tense error. With "have" (present perfect), the past participle "led" is required, not the base form "lead"; Like—
The investigation has led to new discoveries.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. We were returning after an exhilarating day trip to a stunning valley when an experience of a different kind hit us. B. On our recent visit to a Himalayan hill State, we got stranded outside our property for a few hours. C. A huge fallen deodar tree was blocking the path leading to the resort. The local villagers, in a commendable display of solidarity and strength, cleared the path within a few hours. D. It made us realise the hardship and unpredictability of life in mountain terrain. E. But our biggest takeaway here was the spirit of brotherhood that bound these simple hill folks into a symbiotic community.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.

A. We were returning after an exhilarating day trip to a stunning valley when an experience of a different kind hit us.

B. On our recent visit to a Himalayan hill State, we got stranded outside our property for a few hours.

C. A huge fallen deodar tree was blocking the path leading to the resort. The local villagers, in a commendable display of solidarity and strength, cleared the path within a few hours.

D. It made us realise the hardship and unpredictability of life in mountain terrain.

E. But our biggest takeaway here was the spirit of brotherhood that bound these simple hill folks into a symbiotic community.
questions.solution: B starts the paragraph as it introduces the context of the story: a recent visit to a Himalayan hill state where the travelers got stranded outside their property for a few hours.

questions.question: Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank . He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ____ 1 _____ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ____ 2 ____ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any _____ 3 ____ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ______ 4 ____ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ______ 5 _____ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml:
Comprehension:

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ____ 1 _____ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ____ 2 ____ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any _____ 3 ____ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ______ 4 ____ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ______ 5 _____ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution: 'Would' will be used because it indicates a habitual or repeated action in the past. The sentence describes how people regularly shouted his name whenever his car stopped, which makes "would" the most appropriate choice to convey this repeated past behavior. Example: Whenever he visited the market, the shopkeepers would greet him warmly.
